narrative_summary: Summarize case volume, seriousness, dominant patient/geographic characteristics, common reactions, outcomes, and notable time patterns. Distinguish observation from interpretation. Do not make a safety conclusion.
summary_cases: Describe aggregate case volume and patient characteristics using only supplied metrics. Mention missingness where material. For age distribution, do not restate numeric age-band boundaries such as 18-44, 45-64, 65-74, or 75+. Refer to them as the configured age bands and report only their supplied case counts. Every sentence or paragraph containing a number must include the relevant [[E:key]] evidence marker on that same line.
reaction_analysis: Summarize the most frequently reported reactions using only supplied evidence. Report at most the top 10 overall reactions and at most the top 5 serious-case reactions. Keep the section concise. Every numeric claim must have its exact [[E:key]] evidence marker on the same sentence. Never combine multiple evidence keys inside one marker.
serious_alerts: Summarize seriousness and expedite-criteria information conservatively using only supplied evidence. Do not claim that expedite criteria proves a verified 15-day submission. Every evidence citation must use the exact syntax [[E:key]]. If two facts require two citations, write [[E:key1]][[E:key2]], never combine keys inside one marker.
trends: Summarize the reporting trend concisely. Describe the peak month, lowest complete month, and overall pattern using supplied evidence. Do not enumerate every month unless explicitly necessary. Every numeric claim must include its exact [[E:key]] evidence marker.
history_actions: Do not invent regulatory or safety actions. If no action source is supplied, say only that no action information was supplied to this exercise.
